It is the नाभिः (*nābhiḥ*) of Varuṇa, the deity presiding over the night, that is, it stands in the place of the navel: as the navel stays motionless in the middle of the body, so at night it stays in some one place.⟨NOTE:91⟩ O shining chariot-deity, you who are of the qualities stated, accepting this our sacrificial act that gives oblations, accept our oblations.
notes: ತದ್ವದ್ರಾತ್ ಕ್ವಚಿದೇವ ಸಿತಃ: text damaged; read as "at night, stationed in some one place"

en: - रथ (*ratha*)—O god, the presiding deity of the chariot
- वज्रः (*vajraḥ*)—being a part of the thunderbolt
- गर्भः (*garbhaḥ*)—being the one in the middle
- नाभिः (*nābhiḥ*)—being the one who stands in the place of the navel

O shining god, presiding deity of the chariot, you who are a part of Indra's thunderbolt, the leader of the Maruts, the embryo of the god Mitra and the navel of the god Varuṇa, enjoying this sacrificial act offered by us, accept the oblations.
Do you, divine chariot, who are the thunderbolt of Indra, the precursor of the Maruts, the embryo of Mitra, the navel of Varuna, propitiated by this our sacrifice, accept the oblation.

In battle the dundubhi is to be touched with the following tṛca. It is laid down in the sūtra: the dundubhi is to be touched with the tṛca beginning उप श्वासय (*upa śvāsaya*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 3-12-17)⟨NOTE:92⟩. O dundubhi, make the earth and also heaven draw breath: reassure them with your own cry of victory; make such a sound that both worlds are filled with your sound. This is the meaning. Further, all living beings, both the standing (the immovable) and the moving, who stand in their various ways, should in many ways (पुरुत्रा (*purutrā*), that is, बहुधा (*bahudhā*)) take note of your sound; let them know it. O dundubhi, you, united with Indra and the other gods, drive away our enemies from far, from farther than far; make them go away. Here the Nirukta says: शब्दानुकरणं द्रुमो भिन्न इति वा दुंदुभ्यतेर्वा स्याद्वधकर्मणः (*śabdānukaraṇaṃ drumo bhinna iti vā duṃdubhyatervā syādvadhakarmaṇaḥ*) (Ni. 9-12).⟨NOTE:93⟩
notes: abbreviation ಆ. ಗೃ. printed
the bhāṣya reads ಸ್ಯಾದ್ವಧಕರ್ಮಣಃ, the commentary's Yāska passage reads ಸ್ಯಾಚ್ಛಬ್ದಕರ್ಮಣಃ

en: - दुंदुभे (*duṃdubhe*)—O dundubhi, special instrument of war so named
- द्यां उप (*dyāṃ upa*)—the world of heaven (so as to pervade it fully)
- जगत् (*jagat*)—that which is of the nature of the moving; the beings of the two kinds
- दूराद्दवीयः (*dūrāddavīyaḥ*)—even though at the greatest distance
- अप सेध (*apa sedha*)—drive them away and make them vanish

O dundubhi, special instrument of war so named, make a loud sound so as to pervade fully the earth and the world of heaven. May the beings of the two kinds, the immovable and the moving, know your sound in many ways. O dundubhi, the famous one, united with Indra and the other gods, drive away the enemies and make them vanish, even though they be at the greatest distance.

War drum, fill with your sound both heaven and earth; and let all things, fixed or moveable, be aware of it: do you, who are associated with Indra and the gods, drive away our foes to the remotest distance.

In time of battle the dundubhi (the nagāri drum) is to be touched with the tṛca (three Ṛks) beginning उप श्वासय (*upa śvāsaya*), as is explained by the sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Gṛhya-sūtra: उप श्वासय पृथिवीमुत द्यामिति तृचेन दुंदुभिमभिमृशेत् (*upa śvāsaya pṛthivīmuta dyāmiti tṛcena duṃdubhimabhimṛśet*) (Ā. Gṛ. Sū. 3-12-17)⟨NOTE:94⟩.
In the course of explaining the meaning of the word dundubhi, Yāska has given a nirvacana for this Ṛk:

दुंदुभिः । दुंदुभिरिति शब्दानुकरणं । द्रुमो भिन्न इति वा । दुंदुभ्यतेर्ना स्याच्छब्दकर्मणः ॥ तस्यैषा भवति ॥ (*duṃdubhiḥ | duṃdubhiriti śabdānukaraṇaṃ | drumo bhinna iti vā | duṃdubhyaternā syācchabdakarmaṇaḥ ‖ tasyaiṣā bhavati ‖*)

उप श्वासय पृथिवीं च दिवं च बहुधा ते घोषं मन्यतां विष्ठितं स्थावरं जंगमं च यत् स दुंदुभे सहजोषण इंद्रेण च देवेभ्यश्च दूरात् दूरतरमपसेध शत्रून् ॥ (*upa śvāsaya pṛthivīṃ ca divaṃ ca bahudhā te ghoṣaṃ manyatāṃ viṣṭhitaṃ sthāvaraṃ jaṃgamaṃ ca yat sa duṃdubhe sahajoṣaṇa iṃdreṇa ca devebhyaśca dūrāt dūrataramapasedha śatrūn ‖*) (Ni. 9-13)⟨NOTE:95⟩

Dundubhi means the nagāri drum; because it makes the sound dhuṃ dhuṃ, it has come by the name dundubhi. Or else, drumas means a tree; because this is made by splitting and cutting it, it is named dundubhi. Or it may also be derived from the word दुंदुभ्य (*duṃdubhya*), which means making a sound.

O dundubhi, with your sound make the earth and heaven pervaded and filled, that is, let your firm sound pervade the earth and the intermediate region. May all things, of the nature of the moving and the unmoving, or all beings, know you (your sound). And, O dundubhi, you, together with Indra and the gods, make our enemies flee far and farther, that is, very far. This is the main sense of the nirvacana.
notes: abbreviation ಆ. ಗೃ. printed
ನಿ. ೯-೧೩ printed here; the bhāṣya cites the same passage as ನಿ. ೯-೧೨

en: O dundubhi, आ क्रंदय (*ā kraṃdaya*): urge on our enemies. Give us (आ धाः (*ā dhāḥ*): bestow, grant) strength (बलं (*balaṃ*)) in the form of an army and bodily strength (ओजः (*ojaḥ*)). How? Harassing, that is, hurting, the दुरिता (*duritā*), the hard-to-traverse (misfortunes), you thunder aloud (निः स्तनिहि (*niḥ stanihi*): make a sound continuously). The root is स्तन (*stana*), in the sense of sound. O dundubhi, those armies of enemies (दुच्चना (*duccanā*)) whose happiness (शुनं (*śunaṃ*), that is, सुखं (*sukhaṃ*)) is the cause of sorrow to us, drive away (अप प्रोथ (*apa protha*): repel) from this, our place. And you are Indra's fist; like a fist you are the slayer of the enemies. Therefore make us firm, make us strong (वीळयस्व (*vīḷayasva*)).
- बलं (*balaṃ*)—the strength in the form of an army
- निः स्तनिहि (*niḥ stanihi*)—make a loud sound
- दुच्चुनाः (*duccunāḥ*)—the armies of enemies that cause us sorrow
- मुष्टिः असि (*muṣṭiḥ asi*)—you are of the form of a fist

O dundubhi, make our enemies weep. Provide strength in the form of an army, and for our body power of its own. Harassing the enemies of sinful mind, make a loud sound. Drive far from this place the armies of enemies that cause us sorrow. O dundubhi, you are of the form of a fist for Indra. Therefore make us strong.

Sound loud against the (hostile) host : animate our prowess: thunder aloud, terrifying the evil-minded : repel, drum, those whose delight it is to harm us : you are the fist of Indra; inspire us with fierceness.

The first half of this Ṛk has the drum (dundubhi) as deity and the latter half is addressed to Indra. Or else both half-verses are addressed to Indra. O Indra, bring to us (आज (*āja*)) those cows of ours that stand among the enemies; make them come to us. Turn back (प्रत्यावर्तय (*pratyāvartaya*)) these cows of ours that the enemies wish to seize; make them return. And this dundubhi sounds loudly (वावदीति (*vāvadīti*): it makes a mighty sound), केतुमत् (*ketumat*), that is, so as to be known to all. Our men, अश्वपर्णा (*aśvaparṇā*), those who go with horses and who ride horses, move about together (सं चरंति (*saṃ caraṃti*)); they are engaged in fighting with the enemies. That being so, O Indra, may our men who are mounted on chariots conquer the enemies.
- अमूः (*amūḥ*)—our cows that are among the enemies
- आ अज (*ā aja*)—make them come and join us
- केतुमत् (*ketumat*)—so as to come to the notice of all
- सं चरंति (*saṃ caraṃti*)—are moving about on the battlefield

O Indra, make our cows that are among the enemies come and join us. Turn back to us these very cows of ours. This war-dundubhi also sounds so that all may know it. Our warriors, mounted on horses and on chariots, are moving about on the battlefield. May all of them be victorious over the enemies.

Recover these our cattle, Indra ; bring them back : the drum sounds repeatedly as a signal : our leaders, mounted on their steeds, assemble : may our warriors, riding in their cars, Indra, be victorious.
वेदार्थस्य प्रकाशेन तमो हार्दं निवारयन् । पुमर्थांश्च तुरो देयाद्विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरः ॥ (*vedārthasya prakāśena tamo hārdaṃ nivārayan | pumarthāṃśca turo deyādvidyātīrthamaheśvaraḥ ‖*) **GLOSS**

इति श्रीमद्राजाधिराज परमेश्वर वैदिकमार्गप्रवर्तक श्री वीरबुक्कभूपालसाम्राज्यधुरंधरेण सायणाचार्येण विरचिते माधवीये वेदार्थप्रकाशे ऋक्संहिताभाष्ये चतुर्थाष्टके सप्तमोऽध्यायः समाप्तः ॥ (*iti śrīmadrājādhirāja parameśvara vaidikamārgapravartaka śrī vīrabukkabhūpālasāmrājyadhuraṃdhareṇa sāyaṇācāryeṇa viracite mādhavīye vedārthaprakāśe ṛksaṃhitābhāṣye caturthāṣṭake saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ samāptaḥ ‖*) ओं तत्त्वत् (*oṃ tattvat*) **GLOSS**
Here ends the seventh adhyāya, in the fourth aṣṭaka of the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā, which has the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya and a translation in the Kannada language.

यदक्षरपदभ्रष्टं मात्रहीनं तु यद्भवेत् । तत्सर्वं क्षम्यतां देव वागीश्वर नमोऽस्तुते ॥ (*yadakṣarapadabhraṣṭaṃ mātrahīnaṃ tu yadbhavet | tatsarvaṃ kṣamyatāṃ deva vāgīśvara namo 'stute ‖*) **GLOSS** शुभं भूयात् (*śubhaṃ bhūyāt*) मंगळ (*maṃgaḷa*)
ओं (*oṃ*) श्रीः (*śrīḥ*) श्री गणाधिपतये नमः (*śrī gaṇādhipataye namaḥ*)
वागीशाद्याः सुमनसः सर्वार्थानामुपक्रमे । यं नत्वा कृतकृत्याः स्युस्तं नमामि गजाननं ॥ (*vāgīśādyāḥ sumanasaḥ sarvārthānāmupakrame | yaṃ natvā kṛtakṛtyāḥ syustaṃ namāmi gajānanaṃ ‖*) **GLOSS**
यस्य निश्वसितं वेदा यो वेदेभ्योऽखिलं जगत् । निर्ममे तमहं वंदे विद्यातीर्थमहेश्वरं ॥ (*yasya niśvasitaṃ vedā yo vedebhyo 'khilaṃ jagat | nirmame tamahaṃ vaṃde vidyātīrthamaheśvaraṃ ‖*) **GLOSS**
वेदः शिवः शिवो वेदो वेदाध्यायिया सदाशिवः । तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन वेदमेव सदा जपेत् ॥ (*vedaḥ śivaḥ śivo vedo vedādhyāyiyā sadāśivaḥ | tasmātsarvaprayatnena vedameva sadā japet ‖*) **GLOSS**
The Ṛgveda-saṃhitā with the Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya (with the explanation of the translation of the meaning in the Kannada language).
The eighth adhyāya in the fourth aṣṭaka. The forty-eighth sūkta of the sixth maṇḍala.

O praisers, in every sacrifice (यज्ञा यज्ञा (*yajñā yajñā*): in each and every rite) offer praise to Agni, अग्नये (*agnaye*), who is दक्षसे (*dakṣase*), grown great, with every praise (गिरा गिरा (*girā girā*): with speech after speech in the form of praise): this has to be supplied. The word च (*ca*) is to be seen after व (*va*), out of its order. And you offer praise; we too praise him. How is he? Immortal (अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*): free from death), जातवेदसं (*jātavedasaṃ*): the knower of all that is born, or one whose knowledge is born, or one whose wealth is born; dear and favourable, like a friend. Or else, by inversion, वो (*vo*) stands for त्वं (*tvaṃ*), you, and अग्नये (*agnaye*) is a dative in the sense of the object, since the object is an indirect recipient.

The particle च (*ca*) here has the sense of "if". The meaning is this: O praiser, if you in every sacrifice make this Agni grow with every praise, and make him thrive, then we too praise him, who has the qualities of immortality and the rest.
- यज्ञा यज्ञा (*yajñā yajñā*)—in each and every sacrifice
- गिरागिरा (*girāgirā*)—praise with many kinds of praise
- अमृतं (*amṛtaṃ*)—who is free from the nature of death
- प्र शंसिषं (*pra śaṃsiṣaṃ*)—we praise and worship

O praisers, in every sacrifice praise with many kinds of praise Agni, who has abundant power. We also praise and worship Agni, who is free from the nature of death, of born wisdom, and beneficent like a friend.
At every sacrifice (honour) the mighty Agni with your reiterated praise, whilst we glorify him, the immortal, who knows, all things, our dear friend.
As has been said earlier in the application of this sūkta, this Ṛk beginning यज्ञा यज्ञा (*yajñā yajñā*) is to be recited as the stotriya pragātha mantra in the Agnimāruta śastra mantras.
The Aitareya Brāhmaṇa says thus in this matter:

यज्ञायज्ञावो अग्नये देवो वो द्रविणोदा इति मध्ये योनिं चानुरूपं च शंसति तद्यन्मध्ये योनिं चानुरूपं च शंसति तस्मान्मध्ये योनिर्धृता । यदु द्वे सूक्ते शस्त्रा शंसति प्रतिष्ठयोरेव तदुपरिष्टात्पृजननं दधाति प्रजात्यै प्रजायुते प्रजया पशुभिर्य एवं वेद ॥ (*yajñāyajñāvo agnaye devo vo draviṇodā iti madhye yoniṃ cānurūpaṃ ca śaṃsati tadyanmadhye yoniṃ cānurūpaṃ ca śaṃsati tasmānmadhye yonirdhṛtā | yadu dve sūkte śastrā śaṃsati pratiṣṭhayoreva tadupariṣṭātpṛjananaṃ dadhāti prajātyai prajāyute prajayā paśubhirya evaṃ veda ‖*) (Ai. Brā. 1-35)

The hotṛ recites at the beginning of the Agnimāruta śastra mantras the sūkta of the nature of Agni Vaiśvānara, वैश्वानराय पृथुपाजसे (*vaiśvānarāya pṛthupājase*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 3-3). After that he recites, addressed to the Maruts, the sūkta of the nature of the Marut deities, प्रत्वक्षसः प्रतवसः (*pratvakṣasaḥ pratavasaḥ*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-87). For the śastra mantras, after

these two sūktas have been recited, the hotṛ recites the stotriya and the anurūpa pragātha mantras. Here the Ṛk now in hand, यज्ञायज्ञावो आग्नये (*yajñāyajñāvo āgnaye*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 6-48-1), is the stotriya mantra. This is the first pragātha mantra. The Ṛk देवो वो द्रविणोदा (*devo vo draviṇodā*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 7-16-11), recited as corresponding to it, is the anurūpa pragātha mantra. This is the second. In the first pragātha, the tṛca beginning यज्ञायज्ञा (*yajñāyajñā*), there are three Ṛks. These are sung by the Sāmagas (Sāmaveda 35; 703). In response, the ṛtviks of the hotṛ class recite the anurūpa mantras देवो वो द्रविणोदाः (*devo vo draviṇodāḥ*). The reason for reciting these two mantras in the middle of the śastra mantras is this: the Ṛk यज्ञायज्ञा (*yajñāyajñā*), the stotriya mantra, is called the womb (yoni). The two sūktas mentioned above, वैश्वानराय (*vaiśvānarāya*) and प्रत्यक्षसः (*pratyakṣasaḥ*), are the two thighs. Since the womb-region of women lies between the two thighs, in the middle region of the body, these stotriya and anurūpa mantras, of the form of the womb, are put in the middle of the śastra mantras, after the recitation of the two sūktas. By doing so the sacrificer who performs the sacrifice is helped to obtain offspring. The man who knows this also rejoices, furnished with offspring and wealth of cattle.

ऊर्जः (*ūrjaḥ*): of food or of strength; नपातं (*napātaṃ*): the son. "We praise" is to be supplied from the preceding Ṛk by continuation; the meaning is: we praise the son of strength. हिन (*hina*) is a combination of two particles in the sense of हि (*hi*), "for". This Agni indeed is अस्मयुः (*asmayuḥ*), one who desires us. And we would give (दाशेम (*dāśema*): may we give oblations) to that Agni, हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*), the giver of oblations, of offerings, to the gods. And may that Agni be, in battles (वाजेषु (*vājeṣu*): in conflicts), our protector (अविता (*avitā*)) and our increaser (वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)). And may he also be the protector of our bodies (तनूनां (*tanūnāṃ*)), that is, of our children, our sons.
- हव्यदातये (*havyadātaye*)—to Agni, who distributes the oblation to the gods
- वृधः (*vṛdhaḥ*)—as the cause of our increase
- तनूनां (*tanūnāṃ*)—of our sons, grandsons and the rest

We praise Agni, the son of strength. This same Agni certainly desires us, for the good of the gods. To Agni, who distributes the oblation to the gods, let us offer the oblation. May that same Agni be our protector in battles and the cause of our increase. And may he also be the protector of our sons, grandsons and the rest.
The son of strength, for he verily is propitious to us ; to whom let us offer oblations as to the conveyer of them (to the gods) : may he be our defender and of our offspring.

O Agni, you are वृषा (*vṛṣā*), the showerer of desires, or the maker of rain; अजरः (*ajaraḥ*), free from decay; महान् (*mahān*), greater in qualities. Being such, you shine forth (विभासि (*vibhāsi*)) with your flame (अर्चिषा (*arciṣā*)), that is, with your light: you indeed shine in a special way.

O bright Agni (शुचे (*śuce*)), you who blaze exceedingly (शोशुचत् (*śośucat*)) with unceasing (अजस्रेण (*ajasreṇa*)), unbroken splendour (शोचिषा (*śociṣā*): brilliance), shine well (सु दीदिहि (*su dīdihi*)) with beautiful radiances (सुदीतिभिः (*sudītibhiḥ*)): light us up and illuminate us.
- विभासि हि (*vibhāsi hi*)—do you not shine exceedingly
- सु दीदिहि (*su dīdihi*)—blaze exceedingly and spread your light everywhere

O Agni, showerer of desires, free from decay, having exceedingly great qualities, do you not shine exceedingly with your brilliance? O Agni, full of splendour, you who blaze exceedingly with unceasing brilliance, blaze exceedingly with excellent radiance and spread your light everywhere.

Agni, you are the showerer (of benefits), mighty, and exempt from decay, you shine with (great) splendour ; you are resplendent, brilliant (Agni), with unfading lustre : shine forth with glorious rays.

O Agni, you worship (यजसि (*yajasi*)) the great gods: at the sacrifices of the sacrificers you honour them with oblations. Therefore at our sacrifice also, आनुषक् (*ānuṣak*), continuously, in such a way that it goes on without a break,

worship (यक्षि (*yakṣi*)) those gods. For that purpose, with your wisdom (क्रत्वा (*kratvā*)) and also with your action (दंसना (*daṃsanā*)). The word सीं (*sīṃ*) is used in the sense of comprehension: make all those gods face us (अर्वाचः (*arvācaḥ*)), for our protection (अवसे (*avase*)). So also give (रास्व (*rāsva*)) वाजा (*vājā*), foods that are of the nature of oblations; give them to those gods. And you also partake (वंस्व (*vaṃsva*)): enjoy the oblations that have been given to you.
- यक्षि (*yakṣi*)—worship the gods (in our sacrifices also)
- वाजान् (*vājān*)—the foods in the form of oblation

O Agni, you worship the great gods. Therefore worship them without a break in our sacrifice also. With your wisdom and with your acts make all those gods face us, for our protection. Offer to them the foods in the form of oblation, and partake of them yourselves as well.

You sacrifice to the mighty gods : sacrifice (for us) continually, for (sacrifice is perfected) by your wisdom and your acts : bring them down, Agni, for our salvation : present (to them) the sacrificial food, partake of it yourself.

The waters called vasatīvarī, the stones (अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*): the pressing-stones), and the forests, that is, woods and timber (वना (*vanā*)), fill (पिप्रति (*piprati*): make full) that Agni who is within, like an embryo (गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)), of the sacrifice or of the water (ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*)). Or else: the waters of the sea, the clouds (अद्रयः (*adrayaḥ*): मेघा (*meghā*)) and the forests fill that Agni who exists as the embryo of ऋतस्य (*ṛtasya*) in the form of the submarine fire, lightning and forest fire. And that Agni who, churned (मथितः (*mathitaḥ*)) with force (सहसा (*sahasā*): with strength) by the men (नृभिः (*nṛbhiḥ*): by the leaders, the ṛtviks), is born (जायते (*jāyate*): appears) on the earth (पृथिव्या अधि (*pṛthivyā adhi*): on the surface of the earth), in the elevated (सानवि (*sānavi*)) and excellent place of the divine sacrifice: you are he, and वंस्व (*vaṃsva*) is to be construed with it. Or else the connection is with यः पप्रौ (*yaḥ paprau*) of the following Ṛk.
- गर्भं (*garbhaṃ*)—who is of the form of the embryo
- सानवि (*sānavi*)—in the elevated place of sacrifice
- जायसे (*jāyase*)—is born (may such an Agni partake of our oblation)

The waters, the clouds and the forests nourish that Agni who is the embryo of the sacrifice; that Agni who, churned with force by the ṛtviks and kindled, is born on the earth at the elevated sacrificial altar: may such an Agni partake of our oblation.

(You are he) whom the waters, the mountains, the woods, nourish as the embryo of sacrifice : who, churned with strength by the performers (of the rite), are generated in the highest place of the earth.

The Agni who, shining with his radiance (भानुना (*bhānunā*)), fills (पप्रौ (*paprau*): अपूरयति (*apūrayati*)) both worlds (रोदसी (*rodasī*)), heaven and earth, moves (धावते (*dhāvate*): goes) with smoke (धूमेन (*dhūmena*)) in the sky, that is, the atmosphere. For smoke, transformed into the nature of a cloud, goes in the atmosphere; with the intention of not distinguishing cause and effect, that going is figuratively ascribed to Agni. Further, this अरुषः (*aruṣaḥ*), the shining one, वृषा (*vṛṣā*), the showerer of desires, Agni of such qualities, is seen (ददृशे (*dadṛśe*)) on all sides, having put aside (तिरः (*tiraḥ*)) the darkness (तमः (*tamaḥ*)), in the dark-coloured (श्यावासु (*śyāvāsu*)) nights (ऊर्म्यासु (*ūrmyāsu*): this is a name of night). And he stands over the dark-coloured nights (श्यावाः (*śyāvāḥ*)). The repetition अरुषो वृषा (*aruṣo vṛṣā*) is for respect or for filling out the pāda.
- उभे रोदसी (*ubhe rodasī*)—both heaven and earth
- आ पप्रौ (*ā paprau*)—he who stands pervading them
- वृषा (*vṛṣā*)—and the showerer of desires, Agni
- तमः तिरः (*tamaḥ tiraḥ*)—thrusting the darkness aside
- आ ददृशे (*ā dadṛśe*)—is seen on all sides

The Agni who stands pervading heaven and earth with his radiance moves about in the atmosphere in the form of smoke. Agni, possessed of an attractive colour and showerer of desires, thrusting aside the darkness in the dark-coloured nights, is seen on all sides. Agni, the shining one, the showerer of desires, stands having occupied the dark-coloured nights (he shines).
He who fills both heaven and earth with light, who mounts with sm ke into the sky, this radiant showerer (of benefits) is beheld in the dark
nights dispersing the gloom : this radiant showerer (of benefits) presides over the dark nights.

O divine one (देव (*deva*)), endowed with the qualities of giving and the rest, O youngest (यविष्ठ्य (*yaviṣṭhya*)), O bright (शुक्र (*śukra*)) and shining Agni, you who are kindled (समिधानः (*samidhānaḥ*)) with pure (शुक्रेण (*śukreṇa*): निर्मलेन (*nirmalena*)) splendour (शोचिषा (*śociṣā*): lustre) in भरद्वाजेऽस्मद्धातरि (*bharadvāje 'smaddhātari*),⟨NOTE:98⟩ shine (दीदिहि (*dīdihi*): be kindled) for our sake, with great (बृहद्भिः (*bṛhadbhiḥ*)) flames (अर्चिभिः (*arcibhiḥ*): lustres), so as to be endowed with wealth (रेवत् (*revat*)). So also, O purifier (पावक (*pāvaka*)), O Agni who cleanses, shine so that you are joined with brilliance (द्युमत् (*dyumat*): shining).
notes: ಭರದ್ವಾಜೇಽಸ್ಮದ್ಧಾತರಿ: ಧಾತರಿ unclear, perhaps ಹೋತರಿ or ಧಾತರಿ "supporter"; translated only as Bharadvāja

en: - रेवत् (*revat*)—so as to be rich and a bestower of wealth

O Agni, divine one, exceedingly young and radiant, kindled by Bharadvāja with pure radiance, shine with great lustres so that you are rich and a bestower of wealth to our share. O Agni, the purifier, shine with splendid radiance.
Divine, resplendent Agni, youngest (of the gods), when kindled by Bharadwaja, shines with many flames, with pure lustre, (conferring) riches upon us ; shine, resplendent purifier.

O Agni, you are the lord of the house (गृहपतिः (*gṛhapatiḥ*)) of all the human (मानुषीणां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ*): born of Manu) peoples (विशां (*viśāṃ*): the subjects); you are the master of the house. Therefore,⟨NOTE:99⟩ O youngest Agni, protect (पाहि (*pāhi*): guard) me, who have well kindled you (समेद्धारं (*sameddhāraṃ*)), for a hundred winters (शतं हिमाः (*śataṃ himāḥ*): a hundred years), with a hundred (शतं (*śataṃ*)) guardians (पूर्भिः (*pūrbhiḥ*): protectors), from sin (अंहसः (*aṃhasaḥ*)) or from the enemy who strikes. And protect also those who give wealth to the praisers (स्तोतृभ्यः (*stotṛbhyaḥ*)), who give it to the one who makes you kindled.
notes: ಆತಸ್ತಂ: reading unclear; taken as "therefore"

en: - मानुषीणां (*mānuṣīṇāṃ*)—born in the line of Manu
- विश्वासां विशां (*viśvāsāṃ viśāṃ*)—of all the peoples
- समेद्धारं (*sameddhāraṃ*)—me, who have made you kindled
- शतं हिमाः (*śataṃ himāḥ*)—for a hundred years

O Agni, you are the lord of the house for all the people born in the line of Manu. O exceedingly young Agni, protect me, who have kindled you, from sins for a hundred years, together with protections numbering a hundred. Protect also those who give wealth to those who praise you.

You, Agni, are the lord of the dwelling and of all men the descendents of Manu: protect me, youngest (of the gods), when kindling you, with a hundred defences against iniquity : (grant me) a hundred winters, (as well as to those) who bestow gifts upon your worshippers.

O Vasu, Agni who makes others dwell, wonderful and worth beholding, urge riches towards us together with your protection. Of this wealth that is seen everywhere in the world you are the conveyer and leader; for that reason, urge wealth to us. And further: for our offspring (the word used here is a name for offspring), for sons and the rest who are the cause of the family's not falling, quickly obtain a firm footing.
- तुचे (*tuce*)—to sons, grandsons and the rest

O Agni, giver of dwelling, you of attractive form, urge towards us riches accompanied by protections. For you are the leader of all well-known wealth. Quickly cause our sons, grandsons and the rest to obtain a lasting condition and state.
Wonderful (Agni), giver of dwellings, encourage us by (your) protection, and (the gift of) riches, for you are the conveyer, Agni, of this wealth : quickly bestow permanence upon our progeny.

O Agni, you protect our son (toka) and grandson (tanaya) with means of protection that are unharmed by anyone and are unseparated, that is, united (here the root has the sense of separation, and the word is taken as meaning not separated). Remove from us the wraths that belong to the gods, and likewise the injuries that belong to men; set them apart from us.
- आदभैः (*ādabhaiḥ*)—those that are non-injurious, or those that are not injured by anyone
- अप्रयुत्वभिः (*aprayutvabhiḥ*)—those that are always kept together
- आदेवानि च (*ādevāni ca*)—and also those belonging to men
- ह्वरांसि (*hvarāṃsi*)—drive them far from us and make them flee

O Agni, protect our son and grandson with protections that are non-injurious and not injured by anyone. Remove from us the wraths that belong to the gods. Make it so that, if men become angry with us, the effect of it does not touch us.
You protect with uninjurable, irremoveable defences (our) sons and grandsons : remove far from us celestial wrath and human malevolence.

O friends, adhvaryus who share one name, approach the cow that yields sabar (sabar is a name for milk), the cow that gives milk that is the cause of immortality. By what means? With a newer, fresher speech, in the form of a calling-out. After that, set free that cow, the unobstructed one (here the root meaning "to throb" has the sense of killing, so she is one who is not to be hindered), and let her go to her calf. Because the verse is addressed to the Maruts, what is to be supplied is that the milk is to be milked for the sacrifice of the Maruts. ⟨NOTE:100⟩. Or else: the cow is the mother of the Maruts, the speech of the middle region called Pṛśni. O friends, praisers, approach with newer praise that Pṛśni, the cow who yields the milk that causes the birth of the Maruts; and release the unobstructed one.
Release her from bondage; set her free. Such a great cow is the mother of the Maruts; what need then to speak of their greatness? Thus this is praise of the Maruts.
notes: ಕದ್ದೇನ printed after ಆಹ್ವಾನರೂಪೇಣ; the word is unclear

en: - अनहस्पुरां (*anahaspurāṃ*)—her who is free of hindrance (release her from bondage)
- उप सृजध्वं (*upa sṛjadhvaṃ*)—join her with her calf
O friendly priests, approach with newly composed words of praise the cow who milks abundant milk. Join her, who is free of hindrance, with her calf.
Approach, friends, the milk-yielding cow with a new song, and let her loose unharmed.

The cow who has milked for the host of the Maruts immortal-making food in the form of milk, a host that is overpowering and self-luminous; and who stays intent on the happiness of the swift Maruts, who act quickly; and who goes along with happiness-bringing waters of the middle region for the sake of the happiness of others too, coming with the rain-waters (the words describing what she goes with are damaged in the print: horses that go, or waters of the middle region) ⟨NOTE:101⟩: approach that cow; this is the connection with the preceding verse. Here also, as before, a praise of the Maruts is to be understood.
notes: ಹೇತುಭೂತ್ಯೈರೇವಯಾವರ್ಯೆವೈರ್ printed; the reading is unclear

en: - एवयावरी (*evayāvarī*)—moves along with horses (approach such a cow)

The cow who provides imperishable food for the host of the Maruts, powerful and self-luminous; she who is a bringer of happiness to the swift Maruts; she who moves along with happiness-bringing horses: approach such a cow (the mother of the Maruts).

She who yields immortal food to the powerful, self-irradiating band of the Maruts, who (is anxious) for the gratification of the self-moving Maruts, who traverses the sky with (the passing waters), shedding delight.

O Maruts, milk for Bharadvāja, our brother, the twofold. What is that twofold? The cow and food. What kind of cow? One that yields all, that is, one that milks what is pervasive and abundant. What kind of food? Food that is sufficient for the enjoyment of all.
- भरद्वाजाय (*bharadvājāya*)—(O Maruts) for the sage Bharadvāja
- विश्वदोहसं (*viśvadohasaṃ*)—who milks so as to pervade the world
- विश्वभोजसं (*viśvabhojasaṃ*)—that serves for the enjoyment of the whole world
- द्विता (*dvitā*)—these two kinds of sources of food

O Maruts, milk for the sage Bharadvāja two kinds of sources of food. They are these: first, the cow who milks so as to pervade the world; second, the food that serves for the enjoyment of the whole world. (Milk both of these fully.)
Milk for Bharadwaja the twofold (blessing), the cow that gives milk to the universe, food that is sufficient for all.

O host of Maruts, I praise you, such as you are (the words of address are damaged in the print) ⟨NOTE:102⟩. For what purpose? For assigning, that is, for the bestowal and giving of riches. How do I praise you? Like Indra, of good works; like Varuṇa, possessed of māyā, that is, wise; like Aryaman, praiseworthy; like Vishnu, one whose wealth is widely spread. Or else, when the deities named by gender are meant, the words "like" are to be seen as having the sense of "and". ⟨NOTE:103⟩
notes: ವಸ್ತಾಂ printed after ತಂ ತಾದೃಶಂ; the reading is unclear
ಯದಾ ತ್ವಸ್ಯಾ ಲಿಂಗೋಕ್ತದೇವತಾಸ್ತದಾನೀಂ printed; the sentence is unclear

en: - इंद्रं न (*iṃdraṃ na*)—(O host of Maruts) like Indra

O host of Maruts, I praise your well-known host of Maruts, which like Indra has excellent works, like Varuṇa is endowed with wisdom, like Aryaman is praiseworthy, and like Vishnu possesses abundant wealth, for the bestowal of wealth.

I praise you, the (company of Maruts), for the distribution of wealth ; (the company that), like Indra, is the achiever of great deeds ; sagacious like Varuna ; adorable as Aryaman, and munificent as Vishnu.

The word "na" is used in the sense of "now". Now I praise (the verb "I praise" is to be supplied) the might of the host of the Maruts: brilliant, loud-sounding, unassailed, that is, not met by enemies, nourishing, a might in the form of the host of the Maruts. And that host of the Maruts, in the manner in which it would make (the sentence continues on the next page).

It would make for us men, together, hundreds of riches; the particle "ā" is in the sense of conjunction. Or else: in the way that it would make thousands of riches together, so I praise; this is connected with what precedes. And further: may that host of the Maruts bring to light for us the hidden, concealed riches, and may it make riches easy to find for us. But when this Ṛk is taken as addressed to Pūṣan, by its gender, then the connection is: I praise the god named Pūṣan, the nourisher, brilliant like the might of the Maruts.
- सं (*saṃ*)—come into being at one time (for that purpose)
- सुवेदा (*suvedā*)—so as to be easily known

In order that riches in hundreds and in thousands may come into being for us, the sacrificers, for that very purpose I now praise the might of the host of the Maruts: radiant, loud-sounding, unassailed and nourishing.

I now (glorify) the brilliant vigour of the company of the Maruts, loud-sounding, irresistible, cherishing, whereby hundreds and thousands (of treasures) are bestowed collectively upon men ; may that (company) make hidden wealth manifest; may it render the wealth easily accessible to us.

O Pūṣan, run to me; come towards me for protection. O Aghṛṇi, of arrived radiance, run upon the enemy people: those who are slayers, who come against us, who are hostile; oppress them. The root "dru" with the prefix "upa" has the sense of oppressing, as in the passage "as it ran upon the offspring and the cattle of the sacrificer" (Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-1-4). And I, standing at your ear, close beside you, quickly praise you.
- आ द्रव (*ā drava*)—be kind, for protection
- आर्यः (*āryaḥ*)—who fall upon us and injure us

O Pūṣan, nourisher of the world, be kind and turn towards me for protection. O god of exceeding radiance, oppress and drive away the enemies, the most sinful, who fall upon us and injure us. Standing right beside your ear, I quickly praise you.
Hasten, Pushan, to me: (repel), bright deity, (all) deadly assailing foes : close at your side I repeat your praise.

The seer, picturing himself together with his sons and grandsons as a tree that is the resort of many birds, asks that it not be uprooted. O Pūṣan, do not uproot the tree that supports crows; do not oppress me, who am sheltered by many, joined by sons, grandsons and others who are my friends and by many other people: this is the meaning. The particle "hi" is in the sense of "and". Destroy completely the hostile people who are unpraiseworthy, or who proclaim unpraiseworthy sorrow. And further: may the enemy, the impeller, not carry us off. The word "so" (as, in the manner that) is supplied in this sentence, though not heard, because of the connection with "evam" and because the verb is accented. "Grīvāḥ" are the nooses that bind. As hunters lay on the ground snares in the form of nets, nooses, in order to catch birds, and birds are caught by them when so laid, so may the enemy not carry us off by means of devices for binding: this is the meaning.
- वि नीनशः हि (*vi nīnaśaḥ hi*)—destroy completely
- वेः (*veḥ*)—spread out for the catching of birds
- आदधते (*ādadhate*)—in the way in which they catch birds
- एव चन (*eva cana*)—in the same way
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—the enemy who is bent on it

O Pūṣan, do not overturn me, who am the giver of shelter and the nourisher of sons, grandsons and all the rest, like a tree that gives shelter to crows and all other birds, as one fells a tree. Destroy completely the unpraiseworthy enemy peoples. And as nets made of ropes, spread out for the catching of birds, catch the birds, in the same way may the enemy who is bent on seizing me not carry me off.
Uproot not, Pushan, the forest lord, with its progeny of crows: utterly destroy those who are my revilers: let not the adversary ensnare me, as (fowlers) set snares for birds.

O Pūṣan, may your friendship with us be free of hindrance, always continuing in one form; may it be so always. "Like that of the leather bag": as the friendship of the bag with its owner is unbroken, so may it be. What is the bag like? Without a hole, closely joined, containing curds, well filled with curds; the repetition of "containing curds" is to show the abundance of curds. Such a bag is always on the chariot of Pūṣan. Like it, may we also be your friends: thus the seer wishes.
- दृतेः इव (*dṛteḥ iva*)—as your bag is secure
O Pūṣan, as your bag, without a break, holding exceeding curds and full of curds, is secure, so may my friendship with you be without obstacle and everlasting.
May your frindship be unbroken, like (the surface) of a skin without a flaw, containing curds.

O Pūṣan, you stand beyond mortals, that is, men; and by your wealth you are equal to all the gods. Therefore, in battles, look upon us: regard us with a look of favour. In the way in which you protected men of former times, so now, today, protect us.
- देवैः उत (*devaiḥ uta*)—with all the gods
- अभि ख्यः (*abhi khyaḥ*)—look with a favouring eye

O Pūṣan, you are greatly superior to men. By your wealth you are equal to all the gods. Therefore look upon us with a favouring eye in battles. As in former times you protected those who worship you, so protect us now also.
Supreme are you above martals : equal in glory are you to the gods : therefore, Pushan, regard us (favourably) in battles : defend us at present as (you have defended) those of old.

O shakers, O Maruts to be especially worshipped, may that pleasant and true speech of yours, the speech of the middle region, be our guide; may she be the conductor of riches for us. Whether of a god or of a mortal man, of a sacrificer, of a person of either kind, the speech that is praised and that is the guide to desirable wealth is that pleasant and true speech: this is the construction. May she be the guide for us.
- धूतयः (*dhūtayaḥ*)—who make trees and the rest tremble
- सूनृता (*sūnṛtā*)—the pleasant and true speech of the middle region
- प्रणीतिः अस्तु (*praṇītiḥ astu*)—may she be, in our case, the guide to wealth
- देवस्य वा (*devasya vā*)—whether of a god
- मर्त्यस्य वा (*martyasya vā*)—or of a man
- वामस्य (*vāmasya*)—may she point the way to the desired wealth

O Maruts, who make trees and the rest tremble and who are exceedingly worthy of worship, may your pleasant and true speech of the middle region be for us a guide to wealth. May this speech, worthy of worship, whether for a god who worships or for a man, point the way to the desired wealth.
Maruts, agitators. especially to be adored, may your kind and true speech be our conductress; that pleasaut (speech which is the guide) to desirable (wealth) for both gods and sacrificing mortals.

Of the host of the Maruts whose work goes round the heaven at once, like the shining sun, moving all around in the sky: such a host of the Maruts have held a brilliant strength, one that bends enemies down and is worthy of sacrifice. That strength is the slayer of Vṛtra and other asuras; and that Vṛtra-slaying strength is the eldest, the most praised of all.
- द्यां परि (*dyāṃ pari*)—all around the sky
- ज्येष्ठं (*jyeṣṭhaṃ*)—is the most praiseworthy of all

The Maruts, the excellent work of whose host pervades the sky all around, continually, like the shining sun, have obtained a strength that is peaceful, that destroys enemies and that is worthy of worship. That same strength becomes the destroyer of enemies. That same enemy-destroying strength is the most praiseworthy of all. ⟨NOTE:104⟩
notes: ಶಾಂತಿಯುತವಾದುದೂ in the Bhāvārtha; the Pratipadārtha has ಕಾಂತಿಯುತವಾದುದೂ for ತ್ವೇಷಂ

en: Whose functions spread quickly round the heavens, like (the light of) the divine sun, since the Maruts possess brilliant, foe-humiliating, and adorable, foe-destroying strength, most excellent foe-destroying strength.

Heaven was born once only; having been produced once, it stands, and when it is destroyed no other like it is born. The earth too was born once only. The milk of Pṛśni, the cow who is the mother of the Maruts, was milked once only; the Maruts were born from that milk. "From the milk of Pṛśni the Maruts were born": so the Taittirīya (Tai. Saṃ. 2-2-11-4). As heaven and earth are produced once only, so Pṛśni also generated the Maruts with milk milked once only. Beyond that, no other thing is born after it; nothing like it is produced.
- तत् अन्यः (*tat anyaḥ*)—anything other than this
- न अनु जायते (*na anu jāyate*)—was not born in this way
The sky was born once only. The earth too was born once only. The milk of the cow named Pṛśni was milked once only. Nothing other than this was born in this way.
Once, indeed, was the heaven generated ; once was the earth born ; once was the milk of Prisni drawn : other than that was not similarly generated.

I praise the people of good works, that is, the host of the gods, with newer songs of praise. So too I praise Mitra and Varuṇa: Mitra the protector from death, Varuṇa the warder-off of sins; I praise both these gods. What are they like? They desire happiness for those who praise. May those of good strength, Varuṇa and the rest, all the gods, come here to this sacrifice; and may they, such as they are, hear our praises. Here the enumeration of Mitra and the others is only indicative, since the sūkta teaches all the deities; for that reason the word "people" is used first as a general designation.
- मित्रा वरुणा (*mitrā varuṇā*)—I praise Mitra and Varuṇa
- आ गमंतु (*ā gamaṃtu*)—may they graciously come

I praise with new praises the divine people of excellent works. I praise also Mitra and Varuṇa, the bringers of happiness. May Mitra, Varuṇa and Agni, of excellent strength, all come together to our sacrifice. May all of them hear our praises and prayers.
I commend with new hymns the man observant of his duty, and the beneficent Mitra and Varuna: may they, the mighty ones. Varuna, Mitra, Agni, come to our rite, and listen (to our praises).

Agni, the priest, is to be praised in the sacrifices of every people. He is of undaunted action, that is, of work free of pride, or of unconfused wisdom. He is the goer, the lord, of the two young women, heaven and earth. He is the child, the son, of heaven. "Agni was born first from heaven" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-45-1): thus the Nigama. ⟨NOTE:105⟩ Or else: he is the son of the one who praises; so too there is a Nigama: "You become a son to the one who served you" (Ṛ. Saṃ. 2-1-9). ⟨NOTE:106⟩ He is the son of strength, the sign of the sacrifice, shining; Agni, of such qualities, I praise, in order to worship him. The word "I praise" is carried over from the first Ṛk.
notes: abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed
abbreviation ಋಗ್ವೇ. printed

en: - आदृप्तक्रतुं (*ādṛptakratuṃ*)—the one whose action is free of pride
- युवत्योः (*yuvatyoḥ*)—to the two young women, heaven and earth
- केतुं (*ketuṃ*)—the one who makes it known
- अरुषं (*aruṣaṃ*)—the one of attractive golden colour
- यजध्यै (*yajadhyai*)—in order to worship, I praise

I praise Agni, in order to worship him: he who is to be praised in the sacrifices of every worshipper, whose action is free of pride, who is the lord of the two young women, heaven and earth, the son of the world of heaven, the son of strength, the one who makes the sacrifice known, of attractive golden colour.

(I incite the worshipper) to offer worship to Agni, who is to be adored at the sacrifices of every man; whose acts are free from arrogance; the lord of two youthful (brides, heaven and earth); the child of heaven, the son of strength, the brilliant symbol of sacrifice.

This Ṛk is a praise of Day and Night. "Of the shining (Sun)", that is, of the radiant Sun, there are two daughters. By the Sun the division of day and night is made; therefore, since they gain their very existence in dependence on him, they are called his two daughters. They are "of various form" विरूपे (*virūpe*), that is, of different forms, by being white and black. Of the two, one is Night.

Night "is joined" पिपिशे (*pipiśe*) with the stars, that is, she is adorned; the other, whose nature is day, is joined with the Sun. Thus both are adorned, the one with the stars, the other with the Sun. "Mutually opposed" मिथस्तुरा (*mithasturā*): they obstruct each other; night is driven back by day, and day by night, which is their mutual obstruction. Therefore they are "proceeding diversely", moving apart in various ways; "purifying", cleansing everything. Day and Night, being thus, are praised by us: may the praise made by us, worthy to be heard and pondered, pervade them.
- विरूपे (*virūpe*)—the two of white and black form, of various colours
- अरुषस्य (*aruṣasya*)—of the Sun of golden colour
- दुहितरा (*duhitarā*)—of the two daughters, Day and Night
- सूरः (*sūraḥ*)—she is joined with the Sun
- मिथस्तुरा (*mithasturā*)—the two who obstruct each other's state
- विचरंती (*vicaraṃtī*)—the two who move about in different ways
- ऋच्यमाने (*ṛcyamāne*)—the two Day and Night, who are praised by us
- नक्षतः (*nakṣataḥ*)—may they pervade our praise (may they hear it and be satisfied)

Of the two daughters of the Sun of golden colour, who are of various colours, white and black, Day and Night, the one, Night, shines with the shining stars. The other, Day, is joined with the Sun. Obstructing each other in their respective states, moving about in different ways, purifying, praised by us, may Day and Night hear our praise, well known and meditative, and be satisfied.

May the two daughters of the radiant (sun) of various form, of whom one glitters with stars, the other (is bright) with the sun, mutually opposed, proceeding diversely, purifying (all things), and entitled to our laudation, be pleased by the praise they hear (from us).

May our great praise go forward, face to face, to Vāyu; the verb is supplied, as suited to the preposition. What sort of Vāyu? One of great wealth; to be chosen and shared in by all; the filler of his own chariot, or, alternatively, the one who fills the chariots of the praisers with wealth. Then comes the direct address: O Vāyu, to be worshipped in the highest degree, whose chariot shines, your "Niyut" are your own mares yoked to your chariot; you approach them, or else (the root meaning lordship) you are the lord of those mares; you are far-seeing. Being such, you honour the sage, the wise praiser, with wealth.
- बृहद्रयिं (*bṛhadrayiṃ*)—the one of very great wealth
- रथप्रां (*rathaprāṃ*)—the one who fills the chariot of the praiser with wealth
- प्र (गच्छतु) (*pra (gacchatu)*)—may it go forth and reach
- प्रयज्यो (*prayajyo*)—O Vāyu, worthy of the highest worship
- कविः (*kaviḥ*)—the one of far-reaching wisdom, you

May our praise, of great qualities, go forth and reach Vāyu, who has very great wealth, is desired by all, and fills the praiser's chariot with wealth. O Vāyu, worthy of the highest worship, you of radiant lustre and far-reaching wisdom, come driving your horses and satisfy the sage, the praiser, with wealth.

May our earnest praise proceed to the presence of Vayu, the possessor of vast riches, the desired of all, the filler of his chariot (with wealth for his worshippers): most adorable (Vayu) you are riding in a radiant car, and driving your Niyut (steeds); you, are far-seeing, show favour to the sage, (your adorer).

May that chariot, belonging to the Aśvins, clothe my body, that is, clothe it with radiance. That chariot is shining, brilliantly bright, and is yoked with horses by a mere act of the mind. O leaders, O Nāsatyas, who are true in nature, leaders of the true, or born from the nose: by which chariot you go to the house of the praiser, to bring about the desires of his son and of the father, the praiser himself; that chariot, as in the first part, is to be connected with the beginning.
- तनयाय (*tanayāya*)—for the son of the praiser
- त्मने च (*tmane ca*)—and also for the praiser himself
- इषयध्यै (*iṣayadhyai*)—in order to fulfil the desired object
- वर्तिः (*vartiḥ*)—towards the house of the praiser
- मनसा (*manasā*)—by mere intention of its own
- छदयत् (*chadayat*)—may it cover with its radiance

O Aśvin gods, leaders, may that same chariot of yours, which shines brilliantly and is joined with the horses by mere intention of its own, and with which you go towards the house of the praiser in order to fulfil the desired object for the praiser's son and for the praiser, cover my body with its radiance.

May that splendid car of the Aswins, which is harnessed at a thought, clothe my form (with radiance): that (car) with which, Nasatyas, leaders of (rites), you go to the dwelling (of the worshipper) to fulfil his desires for his posterity and himself.

O Parjanya and Vāta, that is, Parjanya and Vāyu, makers of rain, send forth the waters from the "earth", a name of the firmament: the waters that are to be obtained from the firmament, that fill. The latter half of the Ṛk is addressed to the Maruts. O hearers of true praise, sages, Maruts: by the praises of whichever praiser you are praised, for that praiser make favourable the whole world, all beings, moving and unmoving. O "stander" of the world: the singular is meant for the host; O establisher of the world of the moving and the unmoving, O host of Maruts: so it is to be construed.
- जिन्वतं (*jinvataṃ*)—send them forth and pour them down
- गीर्भिः (*gīrbhiḥ*)—by whose praises you are pleased, of such a praiser
- जगत् (*jagat*)—all the wealth, moving and unmoving
- आ कृणुध्वं (*ā kṛṇudhvaṃ*)—cause it to increase

O Parjanya and Vāyu, makers of rain, send forth and pour down the waters that are to be obtained from the firmament. O Maruts, hearers of true praises, givers of stability to the moving world, sages: cause to increase all the wealth, moving and unmoving, of that praiser by whose praises you are pleased.

Parjanya and Vata, showerers of rain, send from the firmament available waters : sage Maruts, hearers of truth, establishers of the world, multiply the moveable (wealth of him) by whose praises (you are propitiated).

In the Anvārambhaṇīyā, the verse पावीरवी (*pāvīravī*) is the Yājyā for the oblation to Sarasvatī. It is so put in the Sūtra: पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः पीपिवांसं सरस्वतः (*pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ pīpivāṃsaṃ sarasvataḥ*) (Ā. 2-8). Further, for the एकादशिने (*ekādaśine*)

This verse is also the Yājyā for the cake offered in the animal sacrifice to Sarasvatī. So it is put in the Sūtra: पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुर्यस्ते स्तनः शशयो यो मयोभूः (*pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuryaste stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūḥ*) (Ā. 3-7). It is used also in the Agnimāruta Śastra. So it is put in the Sūtra: राकामहमिति द्वे पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः (*rākāmahamiti dve pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ*) (Ā. 5-20). "Pāvīravī" is the purifier; "kanyā" is the lovely one; "citrāyuḥ" is the one of wondrous motion, or of wondrous food; "vīrapatnī" is she whose husband is Vīra, that is Prajāpati; or else she is the protectress of heroes. May Sarasvatī, such as she is, "grant", bestow, bear, give our rite called the sacrifice. ⟨NOTE:107⟩ The meaning conveyed by a word is indeed carried out. Further, she is "sajoṣāḥ" with the "gnā", that is, pleased together with the wives of the gods; or else "gnā" are the metres, the Gāyatrī and the rest, according to the Śruti छंदांसि वै ग्ना इति (*chaṃdāṃsi vai gnā iti*) **GLOSS**; pleased together with these, may she grant to me who praise a dwelling that is free of breach and cannot be assailed by enemies, nor by cold wind and the like, and happiness as well.
notes: ದದಾತು ನಾ । ಶಬ್ದೇನ: the words after ದದಾತು read broken; the sentence "the meaning conveyed by a word is carried out" is taken from ಶಬ್ದೇನ ಪ್ರತಿಪಾದಿತೋ ಹ್ಯರ್ಥೋಽನುಷ್ಠೀಯತೇ

en: - चित्रायुः (*citrāyuḥ*)—the one with food of many kinds
- धियं (*dhiyaṃ*)—to us the understanding that teaches the rite
- ग्नाभिः (*gnābhiḥ*)—with the wives of the gods
- सजोषा (*sajoṣā*)—that same Sarasvatī, who is joined with them
- अच्छिद्रं (*acchidraṃ*)—that which is free of breach
- दुराधर्षं (*durādharṣaṃ*)—that which cannot be struck by enemies
- यंसत् (*yaṃsat*)—may she favour us by giving

May the goddess Sarasvatī, who is the purifier, of lovely form, with food of many kinds, the protectress of heroes, bestow on us the understanding that teaches the rite. May that same Sarasvatī, joined with the wives of the gods, favour me, the praiser, by giving a house free of breach and not to be struck by enemies, and happiness.

May the purifying, amiable, graceful Saraswati, the bride of the hero, favour our pious rite: may she, together with the wives of the gods, well pleased, bestow upon him who praises her a habitation free from defects, and impenetrable (to wind and rain), and (grant him) felicity.

In the Anvārambhaṇīyā sacrifice, in the oblation made to the deity Sarasvatī, this Ṛk beginning पावीरवी (*pāvīravī*) is to be recited as the Yājyā mantra: this is set forth by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः पीपिवांसं सरस्वतः (*pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ pīpivāṃsaṃ sarasvataḥ*) (Ā. 2-8). In the sacrifice called एकादशिन् (*ekādaśin*), in the animal oblation addressed to the deity Sarasvatī, this Ṛk is to be recited as the Yājyā mantra when the cake is offered: this is set forth by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुर्यस्ते स्तनः शशयो यो मयोभूः (*pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuryaste stanaḥ śaśayo yo mayobhūḥ*) (Ā. 3-7); and that this Ṛk is to be recited also in the mantras of the Agnimāruta Śastra is set forth by the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra राकामहमिति द्वे पावीरवी कन्या चित्रायुः (*rākāmahamiti dve pāvīravī kanyā citrāyuḥ*) (Ā. 5-20).

In the Ekādaśinī, in the animal sacrifice to Pūṣan, पथस्पथः (*pathaspathaḥ*) is the Yājyā for the oblation. So it is put in the Sūtra: पथस्पथः परिपतिं वचस्या बृहस्पते या परमा परावदिति (*pathaspathaḥ paripatiṃ vacasyā bṛhaspate yā paramā parāvaditi*) (Ā. 3-7). Pūṣan is the lord of every path, the worshipful one. The praiser, who has been brought under his power by the fruit he desires, is to reach him with his praise. And may that Pūṣan give us cows, the ones that check sorrow, "candrāgrāḥ": "candra" is a name of gold, so they are gold-fronted, or gold-horned. And may that Pūṣan carry through every rite of ours.
- कामेन (*kāmena*)—by the desire to obtain the fruit
- कृतः (*kṛtaḥ*)—the praiser who has brought him under his power
- अभ्यानट् (*abhyānaṭ*)—may he approach and reach him
- सः पूषा (*saḥ pūṣā*)—that same god Pūṣan
- प्र सीषधाति (*pra sīṣadhāti*)—may he adorn completely (make fruitful)

May the praiser, who by the desire to obtain the fruit has brought under his power the god Pūṣan, the excellent protector of all paths and the worshipful one, approach him with his praise and reach him. May that same god Pūṣan give us cows with golden horns. May he adorn all our rites completely.

May (the worshipper), influenced by the hope (of reward), approach with praise the adorable (Pushan), protector of all paths : may he bestow upon us cows with golden horns: may Pushan bring to perfection our every rite.

In the sacrifice called एकादशिन् (*ekādaśin*), when the oblation is offered in the animal homa addressed to Pūṣan, this Ṛk beginning पथस्पथः (*pathaspathaḥ*) is to be recited as the Yājyā mantra: this is set forth by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra पथस्पथः परिपतिं वचस्या बृहस्पते या परमा परावदिति द्वे (*pathaspathaḥ paripatiṃ vacasyā bṛhaspate yā paramā parāvaditi dve*) (Ā. 3-7).
Yāska has given an explanation of this Ṛk:

पथस्पथोऽधिपतिं वचनेन कामेन कृतोऽभ्यानदर्कमभ्यापन्नोऽकर्मिति वा स नो ददातु चायनीयाग्राणि धनानि कर्मकर्म च नः प्रसाधयतु पूषेति ॥ (*pathaspatho 'dhipatiṃ vacanena kāmena kṛto 'bhyānadarkamabhyāpanno 'karmiti vā sa no dadātu cāyanīyāgrāṇi dhanāni karmakarma ca naḥ prasādhayatu pūṣeti ‖*) (Ni. 12-18)
This god Pūṣan is the lord of all paths and is to be worshipped by all. May the praiser approach such a god with praise, that is, praise him, for the obtaining of his desired objects. May that god
give us, and favour us with, wealth of many kinds and of the best kind, in every act, that is, in all acts such as the sacrifice and the offering: this is the main sense of the explanation.

In the animal sacrifice to Tvaṣṭṛ, प्रथमभाजं (*prathamabhājaṃ*) is the Yājyā for the oblation. So it is put in the Sūtra: प्रथमभाजं यशसं वयोधां सोमापूषणा जनना रयीणां (*prathamabhājaṃ yaśasaṃ vayodhāṃ somāpūṣaṇā jananā rayīṇāṃ*) (Ā. 3-8). "Prathamabhāj" is the divider of the living beings at the very time of their first origin; so according to the Śruti: यावच्चो वै रेतसः सिक्तस्य त्वष्टा रूपाणि विकरोति तावच्चो वै तत्प्रजायत । (*yāvacco vai retasaḥ siktasya tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi vikaroti tāvacco vai tatprajāyata |*) (Tai. Saṃ. 1-5-9-1) ⟨NOTE:108⟩ **GLOSS**. "Yaśasam" is the glorious one; "vayodhām" is the giver, the bearer, of "vayas", food in the form of the oblation, or else the giver of food to the praisers. "Supāṇi": the part of the hand above the wrist is the "pāṇi"; so he is the god with beautiful hands, endowed with the qualities of giving and the rest. "Sugabhasti": "gabhasti" is a name for the arm; so he has beautiful arms. "Ṛbhvam" is the one who shines widely, or the great one. "Pastyānām": "pastya" is a name for the house; so, of those who dwell in it, he is "yajata", to be worshipped: that is, to be worshipped by householders. "Suhavam" is the one who can be invoked with ease. May Agni, the Hotṛ, the summoner of the gods, the shining one, worship Tvaṣṭṛ, such as he is; may he worship him with this oblation.
notes: abbreviation ಶೈ. ಸಂ. printed

en: - प्रथमभाजं (*prathamabhājaṃ*)—the one who at the time of origin itself makes the divisions of all living beings
- यशसं (*yaśasaṃ*)—the one whose action gives fame
- देवं (*devaṃ*)—the one who is divine in nature
- पस्त्यानां (*pastyānāṃ*)—for all the householders, the worshippers
- होता (*hotā*)—the one who calls the gods

May Agni, the divine Hotṛ of the whole sacrifice, of surpassing radiance, worship the god Tvaṣṭṛ, who at the time of origin itself makes the divisions of all living beings, whose action gives fame, who is the giver of food, with excellent hands, of surpassing radiance, to be worshipped by all householders, the worshippers, and with excellent invocation.

May the illustrious Agni, the invoker of the gods, worship (with this oblation), Twashtri, the first divider (of forms), the renowned, the giver of food, the well-handed, the vast, the adored of householders, the readily invoked.

In the animal sacrifice addressed to the deity Tvaṣṭṛ, when the oblation is offered, this Ṛk beginning प्रथमभाजं (*prathamabhājaṃ*) is to be recited as the Yājyā mantra: this is set forth by the Sūtra of the Āśvalāyana Śrauta Sūtra प्रथमभाजं यशसं वयोधां सोमापूषणा जनना रयीणामिति सूक्तं (*prathamabhājaṃ yaśasaṃ vayodhāṃ somāpūṣaṇā jananā rayīṇāmiti sūktaṃ*) (Ā. 3-8).

Rudra is the "father", that is, the protector, of the world, of all that is born. "Rud" is sorrow; he who drives it away is the lord. O praiser, by day, with these praises, make this Rudra grow; and at night too make that same Rudra grow with praises. And we, impelled by Rudra the wise, great, fair to see, free of old age, of beautiful happiness, such as he is, may we invoke Rudra, praise him, so that it may be "ṛdhak", in a prosperous manner. ⟨NOTE:109⟩
notes: ಋಧಕ್ ಯುದ್ಧಂ ಸಮೃದ್ಧಂ: ಯುದ್ಧಂ "battle" does not fit; read as "prosperous" from ಸಮೃದ್ಧಂ

en: - भुवनस्य (*bhuvanasya*)—(O praiser) of all that is born
- सुषुम्नं (*suṣumnaṃ*)—the one of excellent qualities, that same Rudra
- ऋधक् (*ṛdhak*)—so that he may be prosperous

O praiser, make Rudra, the protector of all that is born, grow by day with these praises. Make him grow at times of night also. Impelled by Rudra the wise himself, may we praise that same Rudra, of great nature, of fair form, free of decay, of excellent qualities, so that he may be prosperous.

Exalt Rudra, the parent of the world, with these hymns by day ; (exalt) Rudra (with them) by night ; animated by the far-seeing, we invoke him, mighty, of pleasing aspect, undecaying, endowed with felicity, (the source of) prosperity.

O ever-young, wise Maruts, worthy of the sacrifice, such as you are, come to the praise of the praiser, the one to be chosen. And, O leaders, Maruts, growing thus in this manner; or else, pervading there in the firmament like the Aṅgirases: the Aṅgirases are the swift-moving rays, and as these quickly fill the expanse of the sky, so you do; or else the Aṅgirases are the seers themselves, and you are swift-going like them. ⟨NOTE:110⟩ Such as you are, you gladden by rain a "not-wondrous" place: a place thickly covered with herbs and trees is "citra", wondrous; in contrast to it, a place devoid of herbs and the rest you satisfy by raining. The word "hi" is a filler.
notes: ಇತ್ಯಾಮುತ್ರಾಂತರಿಕ್ಷೇ: reading of "there in the firmament" uncertain

en: - आ गंत (*ā gaṃta*)—be so kind as to come
- अचित्रं चित् (*acitraṃ cit*)—even the regions devoid of herbs and the rest

O Maruts, ever-young, wise, worthy of the sacrifice, be so kind as to come towards the venerable praise of the praiser. O Maruts, leaders, you who grow in this manner, pervading all regions and swift like the rays, gladden with rain even the regions devoid of herbs and the rest.

Ever youthful, wise, and adorable Muruts, come to the praise of your adorer : thus augmenting, leaders (of rites), and spreading (through the firmament), like rays (of light) refresh the scanty woods (with rain).

"Vīra" is the valiant one, the one who in various ways drives out enemies: to the host of the Maruts of this kind, O praiser, send forth the praise. So too to the mighty one, and to the swift one, the quick-going: to that host send it. An illustration follows: as a herdsman drives herds, and as he at evening time makes the herds go quickly to the stall, to the house, so send the praise quickly: this is the meaning. And may that host of the Maruts, of the speaker, the sage, the praiser, the praise that is heard, the praise that is to be heard, touch his own body, cling to it; may that praise reach the heart. An illustration of the touching: "as the stars the firmament": as the stars touch the firmament, cling to it, so.
- वीराय (*vīrāya*)—(O praiser) to the host of the valiant Maruts
- तवसे (*tavase*)—to the host of the Maruts that is mighty
- स्तृभिः न (*stṛbhiḥ na*)—as, reached by the stars, it shines
- सः (*saḥ*)—that same host of the Maruts
- विस्पृशति (*vispṛśati*)—may it touch and be fully delighted

O praiser, offer praise to the host of the valiant Maruts. To the host of the Maruts, mighty and swift-going, offer praises quickly, as a herdsman sends the cattle to the cattle-shed. As the firmament shines, reached by the stars, so may that same host of the Maruts touch throughout its body the praiseworthy hymn of the praiser, who is a reciter of praise and wise, and be fully delighted.

Offer adoration to the valiant, powerful, swift-moving (company of the Maruts), as the herdsman (drives his) herd to their stall ; may that company appropriate to its own body the praises of the pious worshipper, as the firmament (is studded) with stars.

Viṣṇu, for the sake of Manu, the Prajāpati, who was harassed, injured, by the Asuras, measured the "terrestrial", earth-connected regions, that is, the three worlds, thrice; the word "cit" is for emphasis: he measured with three strides only. O Viṣṇu, of you, of such a kind
While we dwell in the house or in happiness that is being given to us by you, may we rejoice with wealth, with a body free of disease and the like, and with offspring, a son: may we be delighted.
- यः विष्णुः (*yaḥ viṣṇuḥ*)—(O Viṣṇu) you, the all-pervading, who
- त्रिः विममे चित् (*triḥ vimame cit*)—have measured in three parts
- तस्य ते (*tasya te*)—by you, such as you are
- शर्मन् (*śarman*)—we who dwell in the houses
- तन्ना (*tannā*)—with bodies free of disease and the like
- तना चॆ (*tanā cè*)—and with sons, grandsons and the rest

O Viṣṇu, you, the all-pervading, who for Manu harassed by the Asura measured in three parts all the worlds connected with the earth: dwelling in the houses given to us by you, may we attain joy, with wealth, with bodies free of disease and the like, and with sons, grandsons and the rest.
May we be happy in home, in riches, in person, in children, bestowed upon us by you, Vishnu, who with three (steps) made the terrestrial regions for Manu when harrassed (by the Asuras).

"Budhnya": "budhna" is the firmament, and he who is born there is "ahi"; he who goes in the firmament is "ahi". It is said also: अहिरयनादेत्यंतरिक्षे (*ahirayanādetyaṃtarikṣe*) (Ni. 2-17) **GLOSS**. The god denoted by these two words, being praised with hymns, the means of worship, may give us the food well known in the world, together with the waters. "Parvata" is the filler; or else the one who has the joint-like thunderbolt, or the enemy of mountains. ⟨NOTE:111⟩ He too may give that food. So too Savitṛ, the impelling god, may give that food. Further, "rātiṣācaḥ" are the Viśvedevas, the gods who attend upon gifts; may they with the herbs, the sesame, beans and the rest, in which the ripening (oṣa) is placed, give that food. So too Purandhi, of much wisdom or of many works, Bhaga, the one to be shared, the god so called, may he urge us on towards wealth.
notes: ಪರ್ವತಸ್ಯ ಗಿರೀಃ ಶತ್ರುರಿತಿ ವಾ ಪರ್ವತಃ: text seems damaged, "enemy of mountains" is a guess

en: - रातिषाचः (*rātiṣācaḥ*)—all the gods who give generously
- ओषधीभिः (*oṣadhībhiḥ*)—that which is joined with herbs, trees and the rest
- प्र जिन्वतु (*pra jinvatu*)—may he urge us on

May the god Ahirbudhnya, praised with our hymns, give us the well-known food together with waters. May the god Parvata too give that food. May the god Savitṛ too favour us with it. May all the gods who give generously give us that food, joined with herbs, trees and the rest. May the god Bhaga, of much wisdom, urge us on towards wealth.

May Ahirbudhnya (propitiated) by (our) hymns, and Parvata and Savitri give us food with water: may the bountiful (gods supply us), in addition, with vegetable (grains); and may the all-wise Bhaga be propitious (to us) for (acquirement of) riches.

O all gods, give us wealth and a dwelling. What kind of wealth? "Rathya": connected with the chariot, that is, furnished with chariots. "Carṣaṇiprā": the "carṣaṇayaḥ" are men; it is the filler of them. "Puruvīra": "vīrāḥ" are those born of virility, sons and the rest; so, accompanied by many heroes. It is the protector of the great "ṛta", the sacrifice; for the sacrifice is protected by wealth in the form of the fee, on the saying मृतो यज्ञस्त्वदक्षिण (*mṛto yajñastvadakṣiṇa*) **GLOSS**. What kind of dwelling? Ageless, free of old age. By which wealth and dwelling we may overcome the enemies, the rivals, and the hosts of the Asuras, who are "adevī", not belonging to the gods; and likewise the "ādevī", those among whom the gods have come to accept the oblation ⟨NOTE:112⟩, that is, the peoples who perform the sacrifice, which we may reach, attain, by which wealth and dwelling: give such wealth and dwelling. So the construction runs.
notes: ಅಗತಾ ದೇವಾ ಯಾಸು: ಅಗತಾ read as "come"; ಆಗತಾ?

en: - अदेवी॥ च (*adevī‖ ca*)—and the Asura folk
- अभि क्रमाम (*abhi kramāma*)—may we become able to defeat
- आदेवी॥ (*ādevī‖*)—likewise, who worship the gods with oblations and the like

O Viśvedevas, certainly give us such wealth and dwelling, furnished with chariots, nourishing all our people, accompanied by abundant heroes, a protector of the great sacrifice, free of decay, by which we shall be able to defeat our enemy folk and the Asura folk who fight with us, and likewise satisfy the peoples who worship the gods with oblations and the like.

Grant us, (universal gods), riches, comprehending chariots, numerous dependants, many male offspring, (wealth) the giver of efficiency to the solemn rite. and a dwelling free from decay. wherewith we may overcome malevolent man and unrighteous (spirits), and afford support to those people who are devoted to the gods.

O gods, I invoke your mother, the shining Aditi, the one not to be broken, or the deity so named, "of the not poor", for happiness, with salutations or with hymns. So too I invoke Varuṇa, the one who restrains, Mitra, the protector from death, and the god Agni; and these gods I invoke with salutations. So too "abhikṣad": the root "kṣad" has the sense of injuring; he is the one who injures enemies; and Aryaman, very happy: I invoke him with salutations. I invoke Savitṛ and Bhaga with salutations. What need of more? I invoke all the gods, the protecting, guarding ones, with salutations, with hymns.
- देवान् च (*devān ca*)—all the other gods as well (I invoke, praying)

O gods, I invoke with salutation-accompanied hymns, for the sake of our happiness, the goddess Aditi, your venerable mother, and Varuṇa, Mitra and Agni; and Aryaman, the god who injures enemies and is exceedingly happy-making, and Savitṛ and Bhaga as well. In the same way I invoke, praying, all the other gods who are our protectors.
I invoke with adorations, for the sake of felicity, the divine Aditi and Varuna, Mitra and Agni, overthrower of foes, worthy of devotion, Savitri and Bhaga, and (all) protecting divinities.

"O Sumahas, well-radiant Sūrya, impeller of all, take pleasure in the gods who have Dakṣa as their forefather." Sāyaṇa explains that the word "father" in general denotes merely an ancestor, as in the mantra he cites (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-15-3); that these gods have Dakṣa as their forefather is known from another mantra (Ṛ. Saṃ. 10-72-5). Such well-lit gods, shining beautifully, are to be desired in respect of being free from offence: act so that they commit no offence against us. ⟨NOTE:113⟩ He goes on to describe these gods as those who are twice born, that is, appearing as born in the two worlds.

The gods are "ṛtasāpaḥ", touching the ṛta, the sacrifice; "satyāḥ", true, or speakers of truth; "svarvantaḥ", possessed of wealth; "yajatāḥ", to be worshipped; and "agnijihvāḥ", those whose tongue-equivalent is Agni. The construction is: be pleased with the gods who are of this kind.
notes: ವೀಹಿ: Sāyaṇa glosses ಕಾಮಯಸ್ವ "desire", the Kannada gloss has ಪ್ರೇರಿಸು "impel"

en: - द्विजन्मानः (*dvijanmānaḥ*)—those who are born in both worlds
- सत्याः (*satyāḥ*)—those who are of true nature
- अग्निजिह्वाः (*agnijihvāḥ*)—those who have Agni for their tongue; such as are so
- दक्षपित्मान् (*dakṣapitmān*)—those who have Dakṣa for their father
- अनागास्त्वे (*anāgāstve*)—so as to be free of harm

O Sūrya, of exceeding splendour, impel the gods who are born in both worlds, who touch the sacrifice, who are of true nature, wealthy, venerable, and have Agni for their tongue, who have Dakṣa for their father and are of exceeding radiance, to be free of harm towards us.

Radiant Surya, render the deities, who have Daksha for their progenitor, void of offence towards us ; they who are twice born, desirous of sacrifice, observant of truth, possessors of wealth, deserving of worship whose tongue is Agni.

Moreover, O Heaven and Earth, you two make wide, extensive strength. Likewise, O Rodasī, Heaven and Earth, you of good happiness, make a great, vast refuge, that is, a house. Do so that great wealth ("varivas") may be ours. Further, O Dhiṣaṇe, O sustainers, Heaven and Earth, make freedom from evil for us, for our dwelling.
- यथा (*yathā*)—in whatever way it may be obtained, so favour us
- धिषणे (*dhiṣaṇe*)—O Heaven and Earth, sustainers of the world
- क्षयाय (*kṣayāya*)—for the sake of a dwelling-place

O Heaven and Earth, who bring about happiness, produce exceeding strength for us. Build a great house for us. Favour us in such a way that abundant wealth is obtained by us. O Heaven and Earth, sustainers of the world, produce freedom from sin for us, for the sake of a dwelling-place.

Or bestow, Heaven and Earth, vast strength : give us, Earth and Heaven, a spacious habitation for our comfort : so arrange, that infinite wealth may be ours ; remove, beneficent deities, inquiry from our abode.

The Maruts, the sons of Rudra, invoked today, at this time, are to bow to us, that is, to become inclined to us and come. ⟨NOTE:114⟩ They are of this kind: "vasavaḥ", causers of dwelling, and "adhṛṣṭāḥ", unharmed by others. The construction is: when we, placed in battle, whether it be small or great, call upon these Maruts, the gods, then, today, may they bow to us.
notes: ಅಹೂತಾಃ and ನೋಽಸ್ಮಾನ್ಪತ್ಯಾ in the bhāṣya look damaged; read as "invoked" and "to us"

en: - आ नमंतां (*ā namaṃtāṃ*)—let them descend and come

When we, engaged in a battle, whether small or great, pray to these Maruts, the divine ones, for help, at that time may the Maruts, the givers of dwelling, unassailed by enemies, the sons of Rudra, having been called by us, descend and come towards us.

May the sons of Rudra, givers of dwellings, the unsubdued, invoked on the occasion, stoop down to us, inasmuch as we call upon the divine Maruts that they may be our helpers in difficulty, great or small.

Among those Maruts, Rodasī, the wife of Rudra, the shining speech of the middle region, quickly joins; likewise Pūṣan, "abhyardhayajvā", who makes the praisers prosperous and worships, that is, honours with wealth, being the nourishing god, attends upon those Maruts. "Abhyardhayajvā" means one who, increasing, worships (Ni. 6-6), as Yāska says. O Maruts, when you, having heard our invocation, come, then on the path set apart for your going, all the beings that are there tremble. Another mantra says the same (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-39-5).
- देवी (*devī*)—and the shining goddess of speech of the middle region
- अभ्यर्धयज्वा (*abhyardhayajvā*)—he who makes the praisers prosper through the giving of wealth
- प्रविक्ते (*pravikte*)—divided and made ready for your travelling

O Maruts, you with whom the shining goddess of speech of the middle region, the wife of Rudra, is joined, and whom likewise the god Pūṣan, who makes the praisers prosper through the giving of wealth, attends: when you, having heard our invocation, come, then all beings on the path made ready for your travelling tremble with fear.

With whom the divine Heaven and Earth are associated ; whom Pushan, the rewarder (of his worshippers) with prosperity, honours : when Maruts, having heard our invocation, you come hither, then on your several paths all beings tremble.
Yāska has stated an etymology of the word "abhyardhayajvā" in this Ṛk, and has explained its meaning taking this very Ṛk as the example:
अभ्यर्द्धयज्वाभ्यर्द्धयन्यजति । सिषक्ति पूषा अभ्यर्द्धयज्वा इत्यपि निगमो भवति ॥ (*abhyarddhayajvābhyarddhayanyajati | siṣakti pūṣā abhyarddhayajvā ityapi nigamo bhavati ‖*) (Ni. 6-6)

Durgācārya, commenting on this etymology, says: अभ्यर्द्धयज्वा इत्यनवगतं । अभ्यर्द्धयन् अभिवर्धयन् यो यजति । अभ्यर्द्धयतिरत्र दानार्थः । (*abhyarddhayajvā ityanavagataṃ | abhyarddhayan abhivardhayan yo yajati | abhyarddhayatiratra dānārthaḥ |*). The praise of Pūṣan's quality is stated here: he gives to the man who praises him wealth and the like that grow and increase, or he makes wealth and prosperity for the one who praises him so that he prospers. अभ्यर्द्धयतिरत्र दानार्थः (*abhyarddhayatiratra dānārthaḥ*): the word "abhyardhayan" has here the meaning of giving. If one asks what is given, the intention is that he gives things that are dear to the praiser, or wealth and the like that are desired. To make clear the meaning of this word, they have given this very Ṛk as the example.

युद्ध याथ प्रविक्ते अध्वनि भूमा रेजंते (*yuddha yātha pravikte adhvani bhūmā rejaṃte*): O Maruts, when you come, that is, move (blowing with violence), on the path specially marked out separately for your movement, all beings, that is, all creatures, tremble with fear. Describing thus the extraordinary power and might of the Maruts, the commentator has explained the meaning, giving as an example in this matter the Vedic sentence प्र वेपयंति पर्वतान् वि विंचंति वनस्पतीन् (*pra vepayaṃti parvatān vi viṃcaṃti vanaspatīn*) (Ṛ. Saṃ. 1-39-5), whose meaning is: when the Maruts move with violence they make even the mountains, known as immovable, tremble; they bring down the great trees of the forest, roots and all.

notes: no Ṛk number printed in the Saṃhitā or Pada of this verse; numbered 6 following ೫

en: O praiser, worship with a new, fresh, excellent hymn that well-known Indra, who is a hero, mighty, or one who specially impels enemies, and who is the lover of songs. And may he, being praised, hear our invocation, our hymn; and being lauded, may Indra give abundant food. Therefore, Sāyaṇa says, praise him. ⟨NOTE:116⟩
notes: ಸ್ತೋತಸ್ಯಂ in the bhāṣya looks damaged

en: - स्तवानः (*stavānaḥ*)—that same Indra, who has been praised
- उप श्रवदित् (*upa śravadit*)—he does surely hear
- गृणानः (*gṛṇānaḥ*)—Indra, who is praised by us
- उप रासत् (*upa rāsat*)—let him graciously give

O praiser, worship with a new hymn that well-known, valiant Indra, who is pleased by praise. That same Indra, who has been praised, does surely hear our hymns. May Indra, who is praised by us, graciously give us abundant foods.
Praise, worshipper, with a new hymn, that hero, Indra, who is deserving of praise : may he, so glorified, hear our invocation : may he, so lauded, bestow upon us abundant food.

notes: no Ṛk number printed in this window for this verse; numbered 7 following ೬ above

en: "O waters, friendly to men, you give to our son and to his son the unharmed, protecting food ("omāna"; "avati" means he protects, hence "omā" is protecting food). Give also "śam", the quieting of calamities, and "yoḥ", the keeping apart, the separating, of what is to be kept apart." Why? Because you are "mātṛtamāḥ", more than mothers, physicians. How can there be a remedy greater than that of mothers? He answers: you are the mothers, the begetters, of the whole world, of the stationary and the moving. Therefore you are physicians.
- मानुषीः (*mānuṣīḥ*)—you, who are beneficial to men
- मातृतमाः (*mātṛtamāḥ*)—better than the mother who gave birth
- भिषजः (*bhiṣajaḥ*)—as the nourishers of our health

O deities presiding over the waters, you who are beneficial to men, give to our son and to his son unharmed and protecting food. Produce happiness and freedom from sorrow. You are better than the mother who gave birth, nourishers of our health; for you are the mothers of the whole world, all that is stationary and moving.

Waters, friendly to mankind, grant uninterrupted (life)-preserving (food) for (the perpetuatiou of our) sons and grandsons : grant us security and the removal (of all evil), for you are more then meternal physicians ; you are the parents of the stationary and moveable universe.

Savitṛ, the impelling god, who protects, who is "hiraṇyapāṇi", golden-handed, or one whose hand is beneficial and delightful, and who is "yajataḥ", to be worshipped, is to come to us. The god who is possessed of wealth, like the face of Uṣas, to the sacrificer who has given oblations opens up, makes manifest, the desirable riches: he is Savitṛ. This is the construction.
- प्रतीकं न (*pratīkaṃ na*)—like the divine form
- दाशुषे (*dāśuṣe*)—to the sacrificer who offers oblations
- आ जगम्यात् (*ā jagamyāt*)—may he graciously come

May the god Savitṛ, the protector, having a hand of gold, venerable and divine, who, being wealthy, makes manifest the desired riches to the sacrificer who offers oblations, like the goddess Uṣas of divine form, graciously come towards us.
May the adorable, golden-handed Savitri, the preserver, come to us; he, the munificent, who, like the opening of the dawn, displays desirable (riches) to the offerer of the oblation.

"And, O son of strength, O Agni, son of might, today, at this time, bring, cause to come, to this sacrifice of ours the gods who are to be worshipped, Indra and the others. And may I, at your giving of wealth, be always present. Likewise, O Agni, by your protection may I be "suvīraḥ", possessed of good heroes, sons, grandsons and the like."
- सहसः सूनो (*sahasaḥ sūno*)—O Agni, son of strength
- आद्य (*ādya*)—at this time of the sacrifice
- स्यां (*syāṃ*)—may I be a fit recipient
- सुवीरः (*suvīraḥ*)—possessed of excellent sons, grandsons and the like

O Agni, son of strength, at this time of the sacrifice performed by us, cause the gods to come to our sacrifice. May I always be a fit recipient of your gift of wealth. O Agni, grant that by your protection I may be happy, having obtained excellent sons, grandsons and the like.

And you, son of strength, bring back to-day the deities to this our sacrifice : may I be ever in (the enjoyment of) your bounty : may I through your protection, Agni, be blessed with excellent male descendants.

"And, O wise, O Nāsatyas", of true nature or leaders of truth, O Aśvins, you, the well-known ones, come quickly to this hymn of mine, which is joined with acts of attendance. Having come, as you released the sage Atri from great darkness made by the asuras, so, O leaders, deliver us in battle, when it is at hand, from the suffering caused by enemies.
- धीभिः (*dhībhiḥ*)—of me, who am joined with your acts of worship
- अत्रिं न (*atriṃ na*)—as you freed the sage Atri from darkness
